title.narrative: UNDP Support to an Inclusive and Effective National Dialogue Process in Ethiopia
UNDP Support to an Inclusive and Effective National Dialogue Process in Ethiopia

description.narrative:
The expected outputs of the project are:
Output 1: A National Dialogue Commission is established that is independent, trusted, empowered and enabled to engage citizens, including women and youth, and other stakeholders.
Output 2: An inclusive, transparent, gender-sensitive, and participatory National Dialogue is launched in a timely manner that finds broad, if not universal, acceptance among the population and key stakeholders.
Output 3: Potential solutions found for several, if not all, of the most critical issues facing Ethiopia become a part of substantive discussions within the National Dialogue and its follow-up, attracting as well as focusing civic and political energies.

Detta är finansiering till den UNDP-ledda korgfonden för flera intressenter som inrättats för att stödja den nationella dialogprocessen. Detta projekt syftar till att stödja den nationella dialogen, genom den etiopiska nationella dialogkommissionen (ENDC), ett initiativ som allmänt sett ses som avgörande för att hantera en mycket polariserad politisk miljö genom diskussion, närmande och konsensusskapande mellan konkurrerande åsikter och intressen i kritiska nationella frågor. Projektets övergripande mål är att bidra till att lägga de kritiska grunderna och institutionella förutsättningarna för en effektiv, fredlig och konstruktiv dialog i Etiopien.
För att uppnå dessa ambitiösa mål kommer projektet att stödja den etiopiska nationella dialogkommissionen med tekniskt och ekonomiskt stöd som gör att alla röster kan höras och tas på allvar baserat på deltagande av intressenter inklusive de viktigaste politiska aktörerna, samhällsgrupper som etniska och religiösa minoriteter , kvinnor och missgynnade delar av befolkningen inklusive personer med funktionshinder (PWD), ungdomar, civilsamhället, akademin, den etiopiska diasporan, mediarepresentanter och medborgare i stort, över hela landets kebeles och woredas, nerifrån och upp.
Den totala budget som förväntas för att implementera UNDP-stödet till den nationella dialogen under tre år är 35 MUSD och Sveriges bidrag kommer att vara totalt 11 MSEK (cirka 1 MUSD) under tre år med start juni 2023.

This is funding to the UNDP led multi-stakeholder basket fund set up for supporting the National Dialogue process. This project aims to support the National Dialogue, through the Ethiopian National Dialogue Commission (ENDC), an initiative broadly seen as vital for dealing with a highly polarized political environment through discussion, rapprochement and consensus building between competing views and interests on critical national issues. The overarching goal of the Project is to contribute towards laying-down the critical foundations and institutional prerequisites for effective, peaceful and constructive dialogue in Ethiopia.
To achieve these ambitious aims, the Project will support the Ethiopian National Dialogue Commission with technical and financial assistance that enables all voices to be heard and taken seriously based on the participation of stakeholders including the main political actors, societal groups such as ethnic and religious minorities, women and disadvantaged segments of the population including persons with disabilities (PWD), youth, civil society, academia, the Ethiopian diaspora, media representatives, and citizens at large, across the kebeles and woredas of the country, from the bottom-up.
The total budget expected for implementing the UNDP support to the National Dialogue over three years is 35 MUSD and Sweden's contribution will be a total of 11 MSEK (around 1 MUSD) for three years starting June 2023.

description.narrative:
The following are the major results made in the reporting period.
- Participant & Agenda Collection: ENDC has completed participant selection and agenda collection in all regions, including from the diaspora community. The diaspora agenda collection was conducted in six countries. Sweden served as a hub for participants from the Nordic countries, the United Arab Emirates served as a hub for participants from Gulf countries, and the United Kingdom served as a hub for participants from across Europe. In total, 1,163 diaspora members participated in the process.
- Efforts to engage Tigray in the process: the Commission conducted several consultations with stakeholders as a confidence building measure. These efforts bore fruit when the President of the Tigray Interim Regional Administration granted the Commission approval to proceed. Accordingly, the Commission reached the final stages of preparation to launch the dialogue process in Tigray, following the same bottom-up approach applied in other regions. However, the TPLF subsequently blocked the Commission from initiating the process. Coupled with the recent renewed tensions between the federal government and the TPLF, the Commission has now developed a contingency plan, referred to as Plan B, to ensure Tigrays inclusion. This plan involves transporting willing stakeholders to Addis Ababa to conduct participant and agenda selection there. Sida will closely monitor this process, particularly regarding transparency and inclusivity.
- National Plenary: The Commission had planned to hold the national plenary session during the reporting period. However, its decision not to proceed without the inclusion of Tigray is the primary reason, among others, for postponing the plenary until 2026.
- Targeted Consultations to Advance Inclusion:During the reporting period, the Commission conducted various targeted consultations with youth, women, civil society organizations, and political parties to raise awareness about the national dialogue process and promote the meaningful inclusion of historically marginalized voices, which is a positive development. However, womens participation currently stands at 29%, failing just short of the commission's 30% target, hence could be further improved. This is another area Sida will continue to follow closely as the program has a clear objective on gender where women should participate at or near parity.
- Digitalization: The digitalization of the national dialogue process is also advancing. The development of the Data Archiving Management System, a tailor-made platform designed to securely manage and preserve critical records from the national dialogue process, is now 95 percent complete.
UNDP
- During the reporting period, UNDP supported the digitalization of the national dialogue process through the development of the Data Archiving Management System (DAMS). Support included procuring a server and heavyduty scanner and providing technical assistance for data encoding.
- As ENDC prepares for the national plenary, UNDP delivered capacitybuilding training to technical staff, nine commissioners, and advisory committee members on agenda setting and deadlockbreaking mechanisms.
- UNDP also provided logistical support for the Commissions diaspora engagement, facilitating agenda collection across six countries and arranging associated travel and logistics.
- UNDP mobilized additional 2.3 million USD from Demark, Ireland, Spain and Sweden.
